sections.title: Sound of the letter pé
paragraphs: The letter name is (pé) /peː/. Its main sound is a consonant, as in (piros) /ˈpiroʃ/, which means red. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks the air. This letter has two sounds.

sections.title: How to say the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, close both lips tight to stop the air. Release your lips sharply without puffing extra air out. Your voice stays off. For the second sound, make the exact same lip movement. Switch your voice on, so your throat vibrates. Put your fingers on your throat to feel that vibration.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: Usually, this letter makes its voiceless sound, as heard in (apa) /ˈɒpɒ/. A sound change called assimilation happens before certain voiced consonants. Assimilation is a change where one sound becomes more like the sound next to it. In that position, the letter sounds like a voiced b, as in (népdal) /ˈneːbdɒl/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: Do not puff out air when you start this sound. Many say it like the aspirated p in pot. An aspirated sound is followed by a small puff of air. Keep your lips tight and release them quickly, like the p in spot.
